title: Brook Road Builders — Dogs, Trucks, Animals & a Little Scientist (Ages 3–4)
summary: Original single-narrator bedtime stories primarily for ages three to four, featuring Rex the puppy, Gus the bear, Jack the boy scientist, Molly the farm puppy, and their working-animal neighbors. Eleven seasons build Brook Road; Seasons Twelve through Fourteen form the fictional Path to Space expedition, from building Star Harbor to leaving a robotic rover station on the Moon and returning safely home. Season Fifteen closes the series with Jack's fifth birthday, a four-wheeled science wagon, familiar childhood games and a quiet homecoming to Pine Park. A child and talking animals traveling to the Moon is original science fiction, not real spaceflight eligibility or safety advice. Only text between spoken-lecture markers is for narration; all references and caregiver notes are nonspoken.
assumed_background: Primary listener is three years old; age range three to four. Enjoyment of trucks, dogs, bears, animals, construction machinery, and playful 'why' questions. Earlier episodes add recognition but are not essential.

lectures.title: Rex and the Yellow Digger
lectures.description: Rex, Gus and Jack visit the fenced Pine Park construction site and watch an excavator scoop and swing.

lectures.title: Gus and the Gravel Mountain
lectures.description: Gus watches dump trucks tip their beds to leave two gravel piles for the park path.

lectures.title: The Bulldozer and the Pancake Hill
lectures.description: A bulldozer pushes soil into a low mound, which Gus names Pancake Hill.

lectures.title: Rex and the Three Kinds of Tracks
lectures.description: A wheel loader moves gravel; Rex, Gus, and Jack compare tire patterns with paw marks at home.

lectures.title: The Road Roller and the Cookie Question
lectures.description: The crew compacts the gravel path with a roller, while Rex imagines a road-sized cookie.

lectures.title: The First Walk Through Pine Park
lectures.description: Pine Park opens, and the friends walk the completed path and read back Jack's notebook.

lectures.title: A Bark from the Other Side
lectures.description: Rex hears another puppy across the brook. A small excavator begins a walking bridge to Green Gate Farm, and Molly becomes a new neighbor.

lectures.title: The Truck with the Turning Drum
lectures.description: A concrete mixer truck brings material for the bridge supports while Gus wonders whether it is a washing machine for caps.

lectures.title: Jack's Bridge for an Acorn
lectures.description: During the bridge-building wait, Jack, Rex, and Gus compare flat and folded paper over two blocks with an acorn.

lectures.title: The Crane and the Long Wooden Bridge
lectures.description: A flatbed delivers a wooden footbridge deck and a crane truck lifts it onto checked supports while the friends watch.

lectures.title: Molly and the Little Loader
lectures.description: From the farm side Molly watches a compact loader bring gravel while the crew finishes the rails and both approaches.

lectures.title: The Bridge of Two Wagging Tails
lectures.description: The Little Bridge opens. Rex finally meets Molly at Green Gate Farm, and Jack draws the new connection.

lectures.title: The Tractor with Two Big Back Wheels
lectures.description: Molly welcomes Rex, Gus and Jack to the farm hayfield, where Farmer Ruth pulls a waiting wagon with her red tractor.

lectures.title: Gus and the Grass Haircut
lectures.description: A tractor-mounted mower cuts the hayfield grass, and Gus worries that the field has had a lopsided haircut.

lectures.title: Rex and the Hay That Floated
lectures.description: After a drying day, a hay tedder fluffs the cut grass while Rex and Molly try to decide whether the field is waving at them.

lectures.title: Jack and the Long Lines in the Field
lectures.description: Jack notices the rake collecting almost-dry hay into long windrows while Molly makes a maze of imaginary paths.

lectures.title: The Baler and the Little Hay Bricks
lectures.description: A baler gathers dry windrows into small rectangular hay bales while Gus imagines building a house for a giant sheep.

lectures.title: The Hay Wagon Comes Home
lectures.description: Adults load the little square bales onto the hay wagon, Farmer Ruth drives around by the farm lane, and Molly finally visits Rex at Pine Park.

lectures.title: The Tow Truck with the Tilting Bed
lectures.description: Aunt Jo has a flat tire on her yellow work van; a flatbed tow truck carries the van to the red-door garage, where the children meet Ms. Pam.

lectures.title: The Tire That Went Soft
lectures.description: Rex, Jack and Gus learn why Aunt Jo's tire lost its shape and watch Ms. Pam measure air pressure in a replacement tire.

lectures.title: Gus and the Van That Grew Taller
lectures.description: Gus watches Ms. Pam use a proper vehicle lift to inspect and complete the repair of Aunt Jo's yellow van, and the van goes back to work.

lectures.title: Jack and the Little Tire Roads
lectures.description: Jack makes tracks with two toy wheels and discovers why the grooves in real vehicle tires are useful on wet roads.

lectures.title: Molly and the Truck with All the Drawers
lectures.description: When Farmer Ruth's red tractor will not start, Ms. Pam brings a white mobile service truck with tools, tests the battery and gets the farm ready for tomorrow.

lectures.title: Rex and the Truck That Needed a Tiny Repair
lectures.description: Rex's familiar wooden dump truck develops a stuck wheel, and the friends use the idea of a repair garage to solve a much smaller problem at home.

lectures.title: The Truck with a Room on Its Back
lectures.description: Rex, Gus, and Jack meet Dan the donkey and his blue box truck at the new parcel shed; Jack discovers what makes this truck different from Ms. Pam's flatbed.

lectures.title: Gus and the Four Orange Cones
lectures.description: Dan delivers a surprisingly small box of nested orange cones to the garage, and Gus tries to understand how four large-looking objects can fit together.

lectures.title: Jack and the Tube That Waited for Rain
lectures.description: A delivery to Pine Park turns out to be a rain gauge, giving Jack something new to watch and Rex a puzzle about where water comes from.

lectures.title: Molly and the Hens Who Followed the Boxes
lectures.description: Dan takes the long farm road to deliver sacks of proper hen feed, while Molly and Rex discover that the hens want to inspect every box.

lectures.title: Gus and the Truck with Two Wheels
lectures.description: A second farm delivery contains a green wheelbarrow, and Gus discovers that a hand truck and a wheelbarrow are quite different sorts of wheeled helpers.

lectures.title: The Truck That Came Home Light
lectures.description: With the garage, park, and farm deliveries complete, the friends build a toy route from empty cartons and watch Dan return his lighter box truck to its shed.

lectures.title: The Rain in Jack's Little Tube
lectures.description: After the first rainy night since the gauge was installed, Jack, Rex and Gus discover that the empty rain gauge at Pine Park now holds a measurable amount of water.

lectures.title: Rex and the Puddle with a Road
lectures.description: Rex follows a tiny roadside stream with his eyes while Jack compares wet grass and pavement and discovers where the water can go.

lectures.title: Gus and the Truck with the Spinning Brooms
lectures.description: Gus is delighted by a street sweeper with turning brushes, while Rex mistakes the roadside-cleaning machine for an enormous toothbrush.

lectures.title: The Truck with the Elephant Trunk
lectures.description: Rex, Gus, and Jack watch an adult crew clean a street-drain basin using a vacuum truck and a huge flexible hose.

lectures.title: Molly and the Tunnel Beneath the Farm Road
lectures.description: A roadside ditch and its small culvert need attention after the rain; Molly watches a familiar compact loader restore the gravel edge of the long farm road.

lectures.title: Jack and the Map of Where the Rain Went
lectures.description: The friends remember the rain by making a small sloping-tray experiment at home, checking Jack's rain gauge, and drawing a map of the water's several routes.

lectures.title: Rex and the Firehouse with Two Red Doors
lectures.description: Rex, Gus and Jack discover the firehouse on Station Lane, meet Captain Ann, and learn that its two red vehicles have different jobs.

lectures.title: The Fire Engine with Many Pockets
lectures.description: At the firehouse open day, Rex and Molly investigate the many equipment compartments of a pumper engine while Gus looks for a place to store an imaginary enormous biscuit.

lectures.title: Gus and the Ladder for the Clouds
lectures.description: Gus watches the aerial ladder truck put out its stabilizers and extend a nesting ladder during a calm-weather demonstration, and imagines who might live in the clouds.

lectures.title: Molly and the Firefighter in the Big Boots
lectures.description: Molly meets Captain Ann again as the fox firefighter puts on protective gear, and discovers that the familiar person is still inside the very big coat and boots.

lectures.title: Jack and the Water That Took a Turn
lectures.description: Jack watches a fire engine water demonstration at the open day, tracing the path from the engine tank through its pump and a bent hose to a painted target.

lectures.title: The Quiet Trucks on Station Lane
lectures.description: After the open day, Rex, Gus, Jack and Molly bring their discoveries together in a drawing of the newly familiar firehouse and settle into their different homes.

lectures.title: Rex and the First Snowplow
lectures.description: A winter morning changes Brook Road overnight; Rex, Gus and Jack watch a prepared town plow make its first slow pass from the warm blue-step house.

lectures.title: Gus and the Snow That Went Sideways
lectures.description: Gus wonders why the snow moves to the side of the plow rather than marching ahead, and Jack makes a small table-top demonstration after a second pass near Station Lane.

lectures.title: The Truck That Shook the Road
lectures.description: At Ms. Pam’s garage the friends see a municipal material-spreader working at a slippery bend, and compare its tiny falling grains with the much larger snowplow blade.

lectures.title: Molly and the Tractor in a Snow Coat
lectures.description: Molly sees Farmer Ruth give the familiar red tractor a front snow blade and clear the separate farm lane while hens and sheep investigate the changed winter field.

lectures.title: Jack and the Snow That Was Not Even
lectures.description: Jack measures snow on open ground while Gus discovers misleading drifts; Mr. Lee clears a Pine Park walkway with an adult-operated snowblower and leaves a safe path to the bench.

lectures.title: The Road to Pancake Hill
lectures.description: The adult crews finish the neighborhood’s pedestrian approaches, Rex and Molly reunite at Pine Park, and Jack draws where every winter machine worked without confusing the footbridge with a truck road.

lectures.title: Rex and the Road Made of Pebbles
lectures.description: After the winter thaw, Rex discovers a worn strip at the Pine Park entrance. Aunt Jo explains why the small repair needs fresh crushed stone, and Jack starts a new question in his notebook.

lectures.title: Gus and the Rock Cruncher
lectures.description: At the stone yard viewing room, Gus sees heavy stone brought from a quarry to a crusher. The loud machine makes smaller pieces, and Gus considers whether a machine can really have a lunch.

lectures.title: Jack and the Shaking Screen
lectures.description: Jack watches a screening machine send big and little stones to different places. His first guess about how it works is wrong, and a simple sorting demonstration helps him understand.

lectures.title: Molly and the Hill That Grew
lectures.description: Molly joins the yard visit and notices a growing pile beneath a conveyor. The two puppies work out that stone can travel uphill on a belt while the stockpile grows below.

lectures.title: The Truck on the Giant Scale
lectures.description: A wheel loader fills an adult-operated road dump truck from the correct stockpile, and the yard scale checks the cargo weight before it leaves for Pine Park.

lectures.title: The Little Stones Come Home
lectures.description: The loaded dump truck reaches Pine Park by the service lane, adults spread and compact the selected crushed stone at the gate, and Jack connects the season to the park’s original construction in his notebook.

lectures.title: Molly and the Wet Corner
lectures.description: Molly notices an unexpected drip beside the red barn wagon door. Farmer Ruth and Mr. Lee inspect the little side shelter; the main barn and its stored hay remain dry, and the adults plan a focused repair.

lectures.title: Gus and the Truck of Long Boards
lectures.description: A material-delivery flatbed brings new timber and roofing sheets, while Dan brings boxed fixings in his blue enclosed truck. Gus compares board lengths with his own steps and learns why the loads need different vehicles.

lectures.title: Jack and the Wobbly Square
lectures.description: At Jack’s kitchen table, the friends compare a loose square stick frame with one stiffened by a diagonal brace; Jack corrects his guess while Gus invents a house for an invisible sheep.

lectures.title: The Machine with the Stretching Arm
lectures.description: A yellow telehandler uses its telescopic boom and pallet forks to place bundled roof panels on the adult work platform. Molly and Rex observe from the farm porch while Gus tries to guess how the machine reaches up without driving under the roof.

lectures.title: Rex and the Hammer Song
lectures.description: Rex listens to the carpenter’s tools from a safe distance while the adult crew fastens the replacement roof and makes a flashing-and-gutter path for rain. A hen provides the loudest inspection of all.

lectures.title: The Barn Door Stays Dry
lectures.description: A light shower tests the completed side shelter. The runoff follows the repaired roof and gutter away from the wagon door, Farmer Ruth returns her green wheelbarrow beneath it, and the puppies settle into a dry afternoon at the farm.

lectures.title: Rex and the Truck That Took the Long Way
lectures.description: Dan delivers hen feed to Green Gate Farm by the long vehicle road while Rex and friends walk over Little Bridge. Jack notices the routes are different and Gus suggests a public picture map.

lectures.title: Gus and the Town on the Rug
lectures.description: The friends assemble their town from an old cardboard carton, blocks, a towel, and a toy dump truck. The walking bridge and long vehicle road need different lines on a map.

lectures.title: Molly and the Path with No Wheels
lectures.description: Molly catches a missing link in Jack's walking-path drawing. The friends trace the green gate, the bridge, and brook, adding a more faithful foot route before meeting Mr. Lee.

lectures.title: Jack and the Two Lines on the Map
lectures.description: Jack checks his proposed map with Ms. Pam, Captain Ann, and Mr. Fred. He corrects Station Lane's side of Brook Road and distinguishes the road routes, pedestrian bridge, and gravel-yard service lane.

lectures.title: The Sign on the Blue Truck
lectures.description: A compact loader brings gravel to prepared supports while Dan delivers the framed picture map with his liftgate. Mr. Lee and Aunt Jo oversee the installation beside the existing Pine Park sign.

lectures.title: One Long Road Home
lectures.description: At a gentle park picnic, familiar neighbors find their places on the newly installed map. Jack revisits his notebook of earlier projects and Rex returns home by the same road that joins his friends.

lectures.title: Jack and the Moon Beyond the Map
lectures.description: After the neighborhood map picnic, Jack asks whether a path can lead to the Moon. The friends meet owl engineer Dr. Ada and hear about the distant Star Harbor project and a six-person mission.

lectures.title: The Road for the Biggest Trucks
lectures.description: The friends visit the coastal Star Harbor project by county highway. Dump trucks, a grader and a roller begin a heavy-access road for rockets and transporters.

lectures.title: Gus and the Ground That Held a Tower
lectures.description: An excavator, haul trucks and a mixer work on the launch-area foundations and flame trench. Jack compares a toy block on a sponge and a board.

lectures.title: The Crane Taller Than the Barn
lectures.description: Molly watches a towering crane lift steel sections for the assembly complex. A wind check pauses the lift, demonstrating patience.

lectures.title: Rex and the Pipes Under the Pad
lectures.description: The friends observe Star Harbor water suppression testing. Rex connects its pipes to the small Brook Road drains he already knows.

lectures.title: The Room That Could Hear a Rocket
lectures.description: The children tour mission control, meet adult pilot Max, and see Star Harbor ready for incoming rocket parts.

lectures.title: The Rocket That Came in Pieces
lectures.description: A parade of special transporters delivers rocket stages, the return cabin and Moon equipment to Star Harbor for assembly.

lectures.title: Gus and the Engine That Pushed Back
lectures.description: Gus and Jack observe a remote engine test. A reading triggers a calm engineering pause; a measuring connection is repaired and retested.

lectures.title: Molly and the Slowest Giant Truck
lectures.description: A huge tracked crawler moves the assembled rocket to its pad by the special route while Molly notices the care taken with every movement.

lectures.title: Six Seats Among the Stars
lectures.description: Rex finds his fitted seat in the cabin trainer. All six travelers practice restraint, communications, and properly stored supplies.

lectures.title: Jack and the Things That Would Float
lectures.description: Jack practices a simulator checklist, spots a deliberately amber door indicator, and learns that a test can pause without failing.

lectures.title: The Little Ship That Went Ahead
lectures.description: An uncrewed delivery rocket sends Scout ahead. The robotic lander reaches a sunny near-side Moon site with a folded rover and antenna.

lectures.title: When Star Harbor Shook
lectures.description: The Star One launch is delayed briefly by a sensor check, then carries all six travelers into Earth orbit over the sea.

lectures.title: Earth in the Window
lectures.description: The friends travel toward the Moon. Floating toys, sealed snacks and the sight of shrinking Earth give them a new sense of distance.

lectures.title: Four Feet on the Moon
lectures.description: Star One reaches lunar orbit; the six descend in the Moon lander and settle on its four landing legs near Scout.

lectures.title: Rex and the Moon That Had No Smells
lectures.description: Rex discovers he cannot sniff outside a helmet as the suited friends make their first careful visit onto the Moon.

lectures.title: The Little House for a Robot
lectures.description: The friends help adult operators establish a small rover science station; a rover pauses before a rock and then takes a clear route.

lectures.title: The Long Road Home
lectures.description: The lander ascends, docks with the waiting orbiting cabin, and the crew returns to Earth for a parachute-aided ocean splashdown and joyful homecoming.

lectures.title: The Mark on Jack's Door
lectures.description: Jack notices the height marks at home and wonders if becoming five will change him immediately; at Pine Park he discovers he likes both his new Moon drawings and his crooked first truck picture.

lectures.title: Gus and the Biggest Present
lectures.description: Gus wants an enormous gift for Jack, but finds a better-sized surprise: Mr. Lee and Ms. Pam are making a small four-wheeled wagon for Jack's science notebook.

lectures.title: Molly and the Wheel That Wobbled
lectures.description: Molly hears the new wagon clunk and Ms. Pam finds a loose wheel fitting; the adults correct it and test the wagon on smooth pavement and gravel.

lectures.title: Rex and the Game on the Rug
lectures.description: Rex worries that Jack will stop playing with his old toy truck when he becomes five; an afternoon building a cardboard rocket truck together gives him his answer.

lectures.title: Five Candles on Pancake Hill
lectures.description: Jack turns five at a Pine Park picnic. The friends give him the completed red science wagon, and news from Scout's Moon rover arrives while the five candles are blown out.

lectures.title: The First Trip at Five
lectures.description: On his first morning as a five-year-old, Jack pulls the wagon through familiar Pine Park, accepts help when a wheel dips off the gravel, and ends with a quiet sense that more adventures are possible.
